Thanks Aisha. Quick technical note on rotation and in-flight KV cache:

- KEK (Key Encryption Key) rotation: we perform a wrap/unwrap rotation where a new KEK is generated and used to re-wrap the Data Encryption Keys (DEKs) asynchronously. During the attestation window we will not re-encrypt live tokenized payloads; instead we rotate wrapping keys for newly issued tokens while keeping DEKs in the existing wrap until a background batch migration completes. This avoids breaking active sessions.

- KV cache & in-flight context: Redwood's runtime maintains a session-level KV cache for prefix tokens. We ensure cache coherence by version-tagging cached entries with the DEK wrapping version. On a KEK rollover we mark new cache entries with the new wrap version; old entries remain readable until TTL expiry. If you require immediate invalidation, we can run a controlled cache flush during a brief maintenance window (estimated 60–120s depending on shard counts).

- Attestation artifacts: operator-signed attestation PDF, HSM audit extracts (filtered), KMS access snapshot (principals and roles as of the event), and a small integrity log (operator cmd verification). We will redact operator SSH connection details but include session start/stop times and checksums of the attestation artifact.

- FIPS mode: for staging we recommend running in FIPS-mode if you're planning to mirror production cryptographic profiles; otherwise standard mode reduces runtime CPU overhead during peak traffic. We'll run the attestation in the mode you specify.

I'll also post the minimal CLI commands we'll run in the session to the shared drive link Aisha included.

— Karthik

Bob / Alice — confirmed. We've scheduled the supervised attestation for Oct 7 10:00–12:00 PDT and sent calendar invites. Quick answers to your questions:

1) HSM audit extract: typically 2–10 MB for a 48-hour window depending on event verbosity. We'll provide an encrypted archive via our secure transfer link; advance notice if you need an alternate SFTP endpoint.

2) DEK re-wrap backoff: our migration job uses exponential backoff with adaptive concurrency. Default policy: start at 128 concurrent re-wraps per shard, backoff to 64 / 32 if rate-limited by underlying storage or HSM throttling. We'll include the live concurrency metrics in the runbook and a manual throttle knob the operator can use during the session.

3) Signing ceremony: we support a dual-operator signing flow for HSM initialization (two hardware operator keys). For attestation we'll perform the ceremony only if we are rotating root wrapping keys; standard KEK rollovers do not require the dual-hold. If you need a multi-operator witnessing, please let us know and we'll have two operators present.
